shot.prose: The page is a documentation home for a JavaScript framework, and the heading "A no-build, native-ESM web framework" announces that purpose immediately and forcefully — hierarchy is clear in one glance, with the oversized bold heading dwarfing everything else on the canvas. The five stat cards (714 executable lines, 21 KB gzipped, 0 build steps, 0 runtime deps, 0 config files) are a smart second-tier focal point and carry real persuasive weight, though the label text inside them wraps inconsistently — "EXECUTABLE LINES" and "GZIPPED, WITH CSS" both break across two lines while "BUILD STEPS" does too, making each card a slightly different visual density despite identical heights; the fixed-height grid holds, so this is minor, but "CONFIG FILES" wrapping while "0" sits lonely beneath it makes that card feel emptier than its siblings. Spacing between the heading, intro paragraph, stat row, footnote, and code block is rhythmic and comfortable — nothing is cramped — but roughly 230 px of flat gray sits unused to the right of the content column at this 1280 px viewport width, which reads more as dead canvas than intentional breathing room. The sidebar and main content area are clearly separated by a visible border line, and every panel reads as a distinct surface: the white sidebar, the light-gray main field, the white stat cards with their hairline borders, and the dark-charcoal code block all have unambiguous backgrounds. Alignment along the left content edge is tight — heading, body copy, inline code, and code block all share the same left indent without a pixel of drift. The orange link color used for "Versus" and "column" in the footnote paragraph is readable but warm-orange-on-white sits near the edge of comfortable contrast for body-sized text, particularly for users with colour-vision deficiency. No active or highlighted state is visible in the sidebar for the current page, so a reader cannot tell at a glance where they are in the nav hierarchy. The small gray circle at the very bottom-right corner of the sidebar has no label and no recognisable icon — its affordance is completely opaque. The page is entirely text plus a single code block; no illustration, diagram, or screenshot breaks the verbal density, which may undersell a framework whose main claim is simplicity.

findings.where: The left sidebar nav list (Start here, AI, FAQ, Versus, and the CORE/STYLES items)
findings.fix: The item corresponding to this page should have a filled or accented background pill and bolder text, clearly distinct from its siblings.
findings.why: Active label turns accent-orange; current position visible instantly.

findings.what: The gray circle at the bottom-right of the sidebar carries no label or recognisable icon, making its purpose completely unclear.
findings.where: Bottom-right corner of the white sidebar, adjacent to the gear icon
findings.fix: Replace with a labelled button or a universally recognised icon (e.g. a user avatar outline or a theme-toggle sun/moon) so the control is self-explanatory.
findings.why: Needs a template or JS change to add icon or label; CSS cannot supply meaning.

findings.what: Approximately 230 px of flat gray to the right of the content column contributes nothing and makes the page feel off-centre at this viewport width.
findings.where: The right third of the main content area, from roughly the end of the stat cards to the right viewport edge
findings.fix: Either widen the content column to use more of the available space, or centre the column between sidebar and right edge rather than left-aligning it.
findings.why: Layout skill: widening trades dead space for unreadable measure; gutter is correct.
